title: Sorting out problems
goal: Return or exchange something, complain about a wrong order or a botched repair, report what people told you, keep a dispute calm, and report a scam or a lost phone to the police.
intro:
The phone comes back from repair worse than before. The jacket you ordered online arrives in the wrong size. The taxi driver charged you double. This unit is about **sorting it out** — firmly, calmly and in Nepali.

The key skill is **reporting what people said**, because every complaint is built on it: 'you *said* it would be ready yesterday', 'they *told me* to bring the receipt', 'he *asked* whether I had proof'. Nepali does this by **quoting the actual words** and adding **भन्यो / भन्नुभयो**, with **भनेर** for questions and **-न भन्नु** for 'told me to…'. You'll also learn how to stay calm and close a deal: **कुरा मिल्यो** 'agreed'.

vocab.note: Addressed as दाइ, भाइ, दिदी, साहुजी.
From ढिलो "late". ढिलाइ भएकोमा माफ गर्नुहोस् "sorry for the delay".
For things that snap or come apart: टुट्यो "it broke". Glass cracking is फुट्नु.
Partner of बिग्रनु "to break down": फोन बिग्रियो "the phone broke" vs उसले फोन बिगार्‍यो "he broke the phone".
जिम्मा "responsibility, charge": मेरो जिम्मा "leave it to me".
नकराउनुहोस् "don't shout". Also "to call out (of animals)".
माफी माग्नु "to apologise". Compare माफ गर्नुहोस् "sorry / excuse me".
पैसा माग्नु "to ask for money"; for asking a question use सोध्नु.
Slightly formal but used everywhere: समस्याको समाधान.
मलाई ठग्यो "he ripped me off"; मलाई ठगियो "I got ripped off". ठग "con man"; ठगी "a scam".
झुटो बोल्नु "to lie". In speech also झूट.
उजुरी दिनु / उजुरी दर्ता गर्नु "to file a complaint".
प्रहरी चौकी "police post"; a larger station is प्रहरी वृत्त or प्रहरी कार्यालय.
Also "to try to": भन्न खोजेको "what I'm trying to say".

phrases.en: Could I speak to the manager?
You said it would be done tomorrow.
It turns out this was already broken.
There's no need to shout — let's talk and sort it out.
So what do we do now?
I need to file a report.
I left my phone in the taxi.

grammar.title: Reporting what people said and asked
grammar.body:
English changes the words when reporting ('He said he *would* come'). Nepali usually **keeps the speaker's actual words** — same person, same tense — and adds a verb of saying after them. There are no quotation marks in speech; the भन्यो at the end tells you it was a quote.

पसलेले "**भोलि बन्छ**" **भन्यो** — 'The shopkeeper said it would be ready tomorrow' (lit. said, 'it'll be ready tomorrow').
उनीहरूले "**फेरि फोन गर्छौँ**" **भने** — 'They said they'd call back' (lit. 'we'll call').

Notice that **गर्छौँ** 'we will' stays as the speakers said it. The pronouns, too, are the original speaker's: उसले **म** आउँछु भन्यो = 'he said **he**'d come'.

**The verb of saying** agrees with the speaker: (म) भनेँ, (ऊ) **भन्यो**, (उनी/उनीहरू) **भने**, (उनी, she) भनिन्, (तपाईं/उहाँ) **भन्नुभयो**. For complaints, the pluperfect is gold: तपाईंले भोलि हुन्छ **भन्नुभएको थियो** 'you had said it would be done tomorrow'.

**Questions** are reported with **भनेर** + सोध्नु 'ask': मैले के भएको **भनेर सोधेँ** 'I asked what had happened'. For yes/no questions add **कि** (… or not): साट्न मिल्छ **कि** मिल्दैन **भनेर** सोधेँ 'I asked whether I could exchange it'.

**भनेर** also links what someone thinks, writes or hears: पैसा फिर्ता हुँदैन **भनेर** लेखेको छ 'it says (is written) there are no refunds'. Before a noun use **भन्ने**: पैसा फिर्ता हुँदैन **भन्ने** नियम 'the rule that there are no refunds'.

**रे** passes on a message second-hand: म्यानेजर अहिले मिटिङमा हुनुहुन्छ **रे** 'the manager's in a meeting, they say'. And when you didn't catch something: **के रे?** 'what did they say?'

examples.en: The shopkeeper said it would be ready in a week.
They said there was no refund.

examples.native: मैले रसिद कहाँ छ भनेर सोधेँ।
examples.roman: maile rasid kahāṃ chha bhanera sodheṃ.

examples.en: I had heard that the money would come back in three days.
Apparently the manager isn't coming in today.

grammar.title: Told me to…, asked me to…: -न भन्नु
grammar.body:
To report an **instruction or request** ('he told me to wait', 'they asked me to bring the receipt'), put the verb in its **-न** form and follow it with **भन्नु**. The person who was told takes **-लाई**:

पसलेले **मलाई** भोलि **आउन भन्यो** — 'The shopkeeper told me to come tomorrow.'
उनीहरूले मलाई रसिद **ल्याउन भने** — 'They told me to bring the receipt.'

**Told not to**: add न- to the -न form: उहाँले मलाई चिन्ता **नगर्न** भन्नुभयो 'he told me not to worry'.

**Asked as a favour**: use the 'for me' form -इदिनु: उसले मलाई फोन **गरिदिन भन्यो** 'he asked me to call (for him)'. More formally, **-न अनुरोध गर्नु** 'to request to': मैले पैसा फिर्ता गर्न **अनुरोध गरेँ**.

**Watch the difference** between three very similar sentences:
- उसले भोलि **आउन** भन्यो — he told (someone) **to come** tomorrow (an instruction)
- उसले भोलि **आउने** भन्यो — he said **he would come** tomorrow (his plan)
- उसले "भोलि **आउनुहोस्**" भन्यो — he said, 'Come tomorrow' (the exact quote; also very common)

The -ने version is extremely useful in complaints: उनीहरूले आज **पठाउने** भनेका थिए 'they said they'd send it today'.

The causative from unit 35, **-न लगाउनु** 'to make / get someone to do', is the stronger cousin: कम्पनीलाई **बनाउन लगाउनुहोस्** 'make the company fix it'.

examples.en: The police told me to come again tomorrow.

examples.en: My friend asked me to look for his bag for him.

dialogue.title: The repair that went wrong
dialogue.setting: Sujan left his phone at a repair shop in Putalisadak, Kathmandu, to have the screen replaced. He's back to collect it.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: दाइ, नमस्ते। मैले अस्ति यहाँ फोन बनाउन दिएको थिएँ।
lines.roman: dāi, namaste. maile asti yahāṃ phon banāuna dieko thieṃ.
lines.en: Hello. I left my phone here for repair the day before yesterday.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: अँ, सम्झेँ। स्क्रिन फेरेको हो नि?
lines.roman: aṃ, samjheṃ. skrin phereko ho ni?
lines.en: Yes, I remember. The new screen, right?

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: हो। तपाईंले हिजो बेलुकासम्म बन्छ भन्नुभएको थियो, तर फोन गर्दा उठाउनुभएन।
lines.roman: ho. tapāiṃle hijo belukāsamma banchha bhannubhaeko thiyo, tara phon gardā uṭhāunubhaena.
lines.en: Yes. You said it'd be ready by yesterday evening, but you didn't pick up when I called.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: सरी भाइ, हिजो एकदम बिजी भयो। ल, फोन तयार छ।
lines.roman: sari bhāi, hijo ekdam biji bhayo. la, phon tayār chha.
lines.en: Sorry, mate, yesterday was crazy. Here you go, it's ready.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: ला, स्क्रिन त बायाँपट्टि चलेकै छैन! अनि छेउमा यो दाग के हो?
lines.roman: lā, skrin ta bāyāṃpaṭṭi chalekai chhaina! ani chheumā yo dāg ke ho?
lines.en: Hang on — the left side of the screen doesn't work at all! And what's this mark on the edge?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: त्यो दाग त पहिल्यै थियो होला।
lines.roman: tyo dāg ta pahilyai thiyo holā.
lines.en: That mark must have been there before.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: थिएन दाइ। मैले दिनुअघि फोटो खिचेको छु, हेर्नुहोस्।
lines.roman: thiena dāi. maile dinuaghi phoṭo khicheko chhu, hernuhos.
lines.en: It wasn't. I took a photo before I handed it over — look.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ओहो… हाम्रो भाइले खोल्दा भएछ जस्तो छ।
lines.roman: oho… hāmro bhāile kholdā bhaechha jasto chha.
lines.en: Oh… looks like it happened when our boy opened it up.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: त्यही त। अब यसको जिम्मेवार को?
lines.roman: tyahi ta. aba yasko jimmewār ko?
lines.en: Exactly. So who's responsible for this?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ठीक छ, नकराउनुस्। म फेरि स्क्रिन फेरिदिन्छु, पैसा लाग्दैन।
lines.roman: ṭhik chha, nakarāunus. ma pheri skrin pheridinchhu, paisā lāgdaina.
lines.en: OK, OK, don't shout. I'll replace the screen again — no charge.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: मैले कहाँ कराएँ र? भनेको मात्र। कहिले बन्छ त?
lines.roman: maile kahāṃ karāeṃ ra? bhaneko mātra. kahile banchha ta?
lines.en: I'm not shouting! I'm just saying. So when will it be ready?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: भोलि दिउँसो दुई बजे। यस पटक पक्का।
lines.roman: bholi diuṃso dui baje. yas paṭak pakkā.
lines.en: Tomorrow at two. Definitely, this time.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: हिजो पनि पक्का भन्नुभएको थियो नि! ठीक छ, कुरा मिल्यो। रसिदमा लेखिदिनुहोस्।
lines.roman: hijo pani pakkā bhannubhaeko thiyo ni! ṭhik chha, kurā milyo. rasidmā lekhidinuhos.
lines.en: You said 'definitely' yesterday too! OK, deal. Write it on the receipt, please.

culture:
In Nepal, **calm wins**. Raising your voice makes everyone lose face, and the other side will dig in; staying friendly but persistent — calling the shopkeeper **दाइ** or **भाइ**, repeating what was promised (**तपाईंले … भन्नुभएको थियो**) and proposing a fix — usually gets results. Phrases like **कुरा गरेर मिलाऔँ** 'let's talk it out' and **बीचको बाटो निकालौँ** 'let's find a middle way' are the language of a deal, sealed with **कुरा मिल्यो**.

Refunds are rare in small shops; receipts often say **बिक्री भएको सामान फिर्ता हुने छैन** 'goods sold will not be taken back'. Exchanges (**साट्न मिल्छ?**) are much easier to get, especially if you come back quickly with the receipt. Online shopping platforms and ride apps like Pathao and inDrive have in-app complaints and lost-item reports, and a polite message in Nepali gets a faster reply than a furious one in English. Many shops respond to the threat of a bad Facebook review.

For theft, scams or a lost phone, go to the nearest **प्रहरी चौकी** to file an **उजुरी** — you'll need the police report to replace a SIM card, a passport or for insurance. The Tourist Police (११४४) in Kathmandu and Pokhara speak English. Officers will expect **तपाईं** and patience; a cup of tea may be offered while the paperwork is written out by hand.

tip.title: Refund or exchange?
tip.body:
- 'Refund' = पैसा **फिर्ता**; 'return it' = **फिर्ता गर्नु**; 'exchange' = **साट्नु**.
- Ask what's possible with **मिल्छ?** — साट्न मिल्छ? · and what's allowed with **पाइन्छ?** — पैसा फिर्ता पाइन्छ?
- 'Not what I ordered': मैले यो अर्डर गरेको **होइन**.
- Keep it friendly: दाइ / दिदी, and तपाईं.

tip.title: Reporting: … भन्नुभएको थियो
tip.body:
- Keep the **actual words**, then add the saying verb: पसलेले "भोलि बन्छ" **भन्यो**.
- Saying verb agrees with the speaker: ऊ **भन्यो**, उनीहरू **भने**, तपाईं **भन्नुभयो**.
- 'You had said…': तपाईंले … **भन्नुभएको थियो**.
- Questions: … **भनेर** सोधेँ; yes/no with **कि**.

tip.title: Told me to…: -न भन्नु
tip.body:
- Instruction: verb in **-न** + **भन्नु**; the person told takes **-लाई**: मलाई भोलि **आउन** भन्यो.
- Not to: **नगर्न** भन्यो.
- Don't mix up: आउ**न** भन्यो 'told me to come' · आउ**ने** भन्यो 'said he'd come'.
- Make them do it: कम्पनीलाई बनाउन **लगाउनुहोस्**.

sentences.en: I asked them to refund the money.

sentences.roman: wārenṭimā chha bhane kampanilāi banāuna lagāunuhos.
sentences.en: If it's under warranty, make the company fix it.

sentences.native: यो कुर्सी टुट्यो, किनेको एक हप्ता पनि भएको छैन।
sentences.roman: yo kursi ṭuṭyo, kineko ek haptā pani bhaeko chhaina.
sentences.en: This chair has broken, and I bought it less than a week ago.

sentences.native: यो कसले बिगार्‍यो?
sentences.roman: yo kasle bigāryo?
sentences.en: Who broke this?

sentences.native: तपाईंहरूले नै बिगार्नुभएको हो, जिम्मेवार तपाईंहरू नै हुनुहुन्छ।
sentences.roman: tapāiṃharule nai bigārnubhaeko ho, jimmewār tapāiṃharu nai hunuhunchha.
sentences.en: You're the ones who damaged it, so you're responsible.

sentences.native: प्रमाणको लागि मैले फोटो खिचेको छु।
sentences.roman: pramānko lāgi maile phoṭo khicheko chhu.
sentences.en: I've taken a photo as proof.

tip.title: Calm wins
tip.body:
- Shouting (**कराउनु**) makes everyone lose face. Say: **कराउनु पर्दैन, कुरा गरेर मिलाऔँ**.
- Ask for patience: **धैर्य गर्नुहोस्**. Apologise: **माफी माग्नु** (म माफी माग्छु).
- Propose a fix with **भने**: आधा पैसा फिर्ता दिनुहुन्छ **भने**…
- Close it: **कुरा मिल्यो**.

sentences.native: कराएर केही हुँदैन, शान्त भएर कुरा गरौँ।
sentences.roman: karāera kehi hundaina, sānta bhaera kurā garauṃ.
sentences.en: Shouting won't help — let's calm down and talk.

sentences.native: दाइ, नकराउनुस् न, कुरा त गरौँ।
sentences.roman: dāi, nakarāunus na, kurā ta garauṃ.
sentences.en: Please don't shout — let's at least talk.

sentences.native: उसले मसँग माफी माग्यो।
sentences.roman: usle masaṃga māphi māgyo.
sentences.en: He apologised to me.

sentences.native: हाम्रो गल्ती भयो, हामी माफी माग्छौँ।
sentences.roman: hāmro galti bhayo, hāmi māphi māgchhauṃ.
sentences.en: It was our mistake; we apologise.

sentences.native: एकछिन धैर्य गर्नुहोस्, म म्यानेजरलाई बोलाउँछु।
sentences.roman: ekchhin dhairya garnuhos, ma myānejarlāi bolāunchhu.
sentences.en: Please be patient a moment, I'll call the manager.

sentences.native: माफी मागेर मात्र हुँदैन, समाधान चाहियो।
sentences.roman: māphi māgera mātra hundaina, samādhān chāhiyo.
sentences.en: Just apologising isn't enough — I need a solution.

sentences.native: यसको समाधान के हो त?
sentences.roman: yasko samādhān ke ho ta?
sentences.en: So what's the solution?

sentences.native: आधा पैसा फिर्ता दिनुहुन्छ भने कुरा मिल्यो।
sentences.roman: ādhā paisā phirtā dinuhunchha bhane kurā milyo.
sentences.en: If you give me half the money back, it's a deal.

sentences.native: अब के गर्ने त, तपाईं नै भन्नुहोस्।
sentences.roman: aba ke garne ta, tapāiṃ nai bhannuhos.
sentences.en: So what do we do now? You tell me.

lessons.title: Scams, lost phones and the police

tip.title: It happened to me: -इयो
tip.body:
- Nepali often reports bad luck without saying who did it, with **-इयो**: मलाई **ठगियो** 'I got ripped off', फोन **भेटियो** 'the phone was found', भेटिएन 'wasn't found'.
- Who did it: **-ले** + active verb: ड्राइभरले मलाई **ठग्यो**.
- At the police: **उजुरी दर्ता गर्नु छ** 'I need to file a report'.
- What the police said: … **भन्नुभयो** / **भने**.

sentences.native: ड्राइभरले मलाई ठग्यो, हजार रुपैयाँ लियो।
sentences.roman: ḍrāibharle malāi ṭhagyo, hajār rupaiyāṃ liyo.
sentences.en: The driver ripped me off — he took a thousand rupees.

sentences.native: अनलाइनमा पैसा तिरेँ, तर सामान आएन, मलाई ठगियो।
sentences.roman: anlāinmā paisā tireṃ, tara sāmān āena, malāi ṭhagiyo.
sentences.en: I paid online but nothing came — I've been scammed.

sentences.native: उसले मसँग झुटो बोल्यो।
sentences.roman: usle masaṃga jhuṭo bolyo.
sentences.en: He lied to me.

sentences.native: यो झुटो कुरा हो, मैले त्यसो भनेकै छैन।
sentences.roman: yo jhuṭo kurā ho, maile tyaso bhanekai chhaina.
sentences.en: That's a lie — I never said that.

sentences.native: नजिकको प्रहरी चौकी कहाँ छ?
sentences.roman: najikko prahari chauki kahāṃ chha?
sentences.en: Where's the nearest police post?

sentences.native: फोन हराएको उजुरी दर्ता गर्नु छ।
sentences.roman: phon harāeko ujuri dartā garnu chha.
sentences.en: I need to report a lost phone.

sentences.native: प्रहरीले सीसीटीभी हेर्छौँ भने।
sentences.roman: praharile sisiṭibhi herchhauṃ bhane.
sentences.en: The police said they'd check the CCTV.

sentences.native: मैले फोन सबैतिर खोजेँ, तर भेटिएन।
sentences.roman: maile phon sabaitira khojeṃ, tara bheṭiena.
sentences.en: I looked for the phone everywhere, but it hasn't turned up.

sentences.native: मेरो झोला पठाओमा छुट्यो, ड्राइभरलाई सम्पर्क गर्न मिल्छ?
sentences.roman: mero jholā Paṭhāomā chhuṭyo, ḍrāibharlāi samparka garna milchha?
sentences.en: I left my bag on a Pathao ride — can I contact the driver?

sentences.native: प्रहरीले मलाई भोलि चौकी आउन भन्नुभयो।
sentences.roman: praharile malāi bholi chauki āuna bhannubhayo.
sentences.en: The police told me to come to the station tomorrow.
